newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean students battle riot police in Seoul.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean students battle riot police in Seoul.

text.p: South Korean riot police on Friday fired volleys of tear gas at about 500 students demanding the resignation of President Kim Young-sam and the arrest of his son, witnesses said.

The students at Seoul's Hanyang University were wielding steel pipes and hurling molotov cocktails in a protest against a corruption scandal that has shattered Kim's reputation and involved his second son, Kim Hyun-chul.
At least one student was beaten and dragged away by police, and several others were detained, witnesses said.
Protesters also demanded the release of about 10 colleagues detained by police on Thursday. Those detained are members of a militant student body with pro-Pyongang sympathies.

The riot came on the eve of the anniversary of massive demonstrations in 1960 that toppled South Korea's first president, Syngman Rhee. The anniversary is often marked by violent clashes between students and police.
Several of president Kim's closest aides are on trial for corruption in connection with a loans scandal surrounding the collapse in January of Hanbo Steel Co, the country's second-largest steelmaker.
